text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Eastern Slavonia elections: many people prevented from voting, elections extended for another day.
- 6.3% federal budget shortfall in 1996 affected mainly Yugoslav Army.
- Belgrade hotels capacity utilization just 22.3% in the first three months of 1997.
NASA BORBA
- Split in Serbian opposition coalition Zajedno (Together): leaders at odds over proposal to expand alliance with other political forces.

- Serb member in Bosnian presidency Momcilo Krajisnik says Bosnian Serb Republic has a right to establish confederal ties and military cooperation with Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the same manner as Bosnia's Moslems and Croats have already done with Croatia.
- Montenegro's Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic might bow to demands by his Democratic Party of Socialists to sack some ministers, but only in the form of a major government reshuffle.
- Montenegrin officials say 5,300-metre explorative bore off Ulcinj on coast has yielded promising results in search for oil in Adriatic Sea.
- Serbian Pensioners' Organisation says that owing to their very low incomes, only 5% of all pensioners will be able to purchase shares as foreseen by ownership transformation bill.
- Fully 88 of the 109 banks in Yugoslavia were in the red on April 7.
- Yugoslav automotive manufacturer Zastava, formely associated only with FIAT, tests Peugeot engines in its cars.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian government authorised imports of up to 50,000 tonnes of fertilizer for spring sowing; farmers freed of all tax obligations for six months.
- Serbian government to divert 200 million dinars to Zmaj, IMT and 21. maj to help produce 2,200 agricultural tractors, 150 combine harvesters and 200 corn harvesters by end of June.
- Proposed law on concessions expected to attract foreign capital; concession time limit will be 30 years.
DEMOKRATIJA
- Montenegrin ruling party makes another attempt to discipline renegade republican prime minister Milo Djukanovic.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- International Monetary Fund delegation expected to visit Belgrade in May to look into situation and talk to authorities, opposition.
- Belgrade University students wind up week-long action to scrub city clean with symbolic march and 'purification' of regime-controlled media houses.
